Research indicates that resistance training alone is insufficient for increasing capillarization; only concurrent training enhances such adaptations (73). As discussed, however, the intensity and duration of aerobic training must be considered in conjunction with the volume of resistance training performed so that the negative effects of nonfunctional overreaching/overtraining do not override potential benefits of enhanced angiogenesis. Moreover, order of scheduling needs to be taken into account as well, with sufficient recovery intervals afforded between aerobic and resistance exercise bouts.
